quiz.0.question: What is the most direct and widespread effect of global warming on Italian wine styles?
quiz.0.options.1: Higher alcohol levels from riper, more sugar-rich grapes — and reduced natural acidity
quiz.0.explanation: Warmer temperatures accelerate sugar ripening faster than phenolic maturity — producing wines with higher alcohol while natural acidity decreases. This is the most immediate and universal impact of climate change on Italian wine.
quiz.1.question: To adapt to climate change heat and drought, what is one of the most common vineyard management strategies adopted by Italian estates?
quiz.1.options.1: Moving vineyards to higher elevations or cooler north-facing slopes
quiz.1.options.3: Installing artificial irrigation regardless of regulations
quiz.1.explanation: Higher elevations are cooler — allowing grapes to ripen more slowly and retain more natural acidity. Many Italian producers are increasingly planting at higher altitudes to offset warming temperatures.
quiz.2.question: In the traditional Barolo appellation, which aspect (slope orientation) was once most prized, and what aspects are now being reassessed because of climate change?
quiz.2.options.0: South-facing was prized; now east-facing is reassessed
quiz.2.options.1: South and southwest-facing slopes were once the most coveted; now cooler north and east-facing slopes are gaining value
quiz.2.options.2: No aspect was ever particularly valued
quiz.2.explanation: Historically, south and southwest-facing Barolo slopes commanded the highest prices (maximum sun exposure). As temperatures rise, these plots risk over-ripening — making once-overlooked cooler north and east-facing sites increasingly attractive.
quiz.3.question: Which of the following is NOT a common winemaking adaptation strategy for climate change?
quiz.3.options.0: Earlier harvesting to preserve natural acidity
quiz.3.options.2: Removing large amounts of water from the wine using reverse osmosis
quiz.3.options.3: Night-time harvesting to preserve aromatic freshness
quiz.3.explanation: While earlier harvesting, acidification and night harvesting are all legitimate and widely used adaptation strategies, excessive use of concentration techniques (reverse osmosis, spinning cone) to fix structural imbalances from over-ripening is generally considered a less desirable 'correction' rather than adaptation.
